To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The persistence of insecticides on soil surfaces and in soil is affected by the pH of both soil and water; and 2) The persistence of many insecticides in soil can be predicted by the pH-dependent persistence in aqueous solution, but the persistence of other insecticides cannot be predicted.
the persistence of insecticide is affected by pH in solution and that this effect cannot be predicted for insecticides applied to soils.
the pH of the medium affects the rate of disappearance (half-life) of insecticides in aqueous solutions, but not on soil surfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of pH on the disappearance of pesticides.
the effect of soil pH on the degradation of pesticides in soil and on the persistence of pesticides in aqueous systems.
the influence of water pH on the persistence and degradation of selected insecticides in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soil and water pH do affect the persistence of insecticide in the soil environment.
soil pH is not a good predictor of insecticide persistence.
pH is a factor of considerable importance to the persistence of insecticide in solution, but its effect is difficult to quantify and is not necessarily predictable in the field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pH dependence of insecticide disappearance is a complex phenomenon that is dependent not only on the chemical structure of the insecticide but also on the nature of the solid phase to which the insecticide is applied.
the persistence of most insecticides is affected by the pH of the aqueous phase, but that this effect is not readily predictable from the pH of the soil or solid phase.

the pH of the soil is not a major factor affecting the persistence of most insecticides, and that the persistence of insecticide in soil is determined primarily by the nature of the soil and the nature of the pesticide itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH-disappearance rate profile in homogeneous solution is a useful tool for understanding the pH dependent disappearance of pesticides in heterogeneous systems.
the persistence of an insecticide in the field cannot be predicted solely from the pH dependent disappearance in water or on a solid.
insecticide disappearance rates on soils are influenced by many factors in addition to pH.
